general_background.title: Precursor delivery and surface chemistry
general_background.summary: Vapour-deposition methods separate precursor delivery from reactions at or near a surface. Adsorbed precursors can react, exchange ligands or desorb, with surface coverage and delivery affecting which processes dominate.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Phosphines and precursor solutions
general_background.summary: Elemental selenium can react with organophosphines to form soluble phosphorus-selenium-containing precursor species. Organic substituents can make these species compatible with an organic medium, while their composition and reactivity depend on the phosphine and preparation conditions.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Phosphine-oxide coordination
general_background.summary: A phosphine oxide can interact with suitable precursor or surface sites through its oxygen donor. Competition among oxygen-donor ligands can change precursor coordination and the availability of surface sites.
